rows.en:
(Staying up late made me hungry...
I need something to eat...)
Huh? \p-kun?

Oh, Akimizu.
What are you doing out at this hour?
Huh? Oh, um, just... some shopping...
I see. A late-night snack, maybe?

Wh-What makes you think that!?
...I mean, it is, but...
rows.notes: Sonna koto!? ...aru kedo: she starts to deny it, then admits it.

rows.en: Oh, I know... something sweet?

...Yes... I just got a craving...
...for some chocolate...
Ahaha, that's such a girl thing.

(It's nothing she needs to be
so embarrassed about, though.)

(Staying up late made me hungry~...
I need something to eat...)
Huh? \p-chan?

Oh, Yuu.
What are you doing out at this hour?
I seeee. A late-night snack, maybe?
Oh, I know... something sweet, right?
Ahaha, that's so you, Yuu.

(But it's nothing she needs to be
so embarrassed about.)
\p-kun! You're safe!
You too, Akimizu.
I made it out okay, but the city...
...Yeah. It's in terrible shape...

I keep thinking... I wish I could've
fought them myself...

I don't want them to do this to us
ever again!
rows.notes: Mou kore ijou wa yararetakunai: 'them' = the attackers, unnamed in the scene; shared male/female.

rows.en: Yeah, I won't let them do any more!
(Next time, for sure...)
\p-chan! You're safe!
You too, Yuu.
I managed somehow, but the city...
...Yeah. It's in terrible shape...
Yeah, I won't let them do any more!

(Well, the exams are over.
Time to take a breather.)
Good work, \p-kun.
rows.notes: Used three times: opening greeting of the male branch, and a closing line in both branches; in the female branch the Japanese has -kun to the female player (the female opening uses -chan, c20456). Kept '-kun' as written; the closing use looks like a script slip.

rows.en:
Oh, good work to you too, Akimizu.
How did your tests go?

Hmmm...
I don't think I did badly, but I can't tell yet.

But your grades always seem to be
near the top...
No, that was just luck, pure luck!
So modest. That's just like you, Akimizu.
Oh, come on! It really was just luck!

(Akimizu's so diligent,
no wonder her grades are good.)

(Well, the exams are over.
Time to take a breather.)
Good work, \p-chan.

Oh, good work to you too, Yuu.
How did your tests go?
So modest. That's just like you, Yuu.

(Yuu's so diligent,
no wonder her grades are good.)

(Well, it's almost lunchtime.
What should I have...?)

\p-kun,
what's wrong? You look like you're
worried about something.

Yeah, I was just wondering
what to eat for lunch...
Ahaha, you sure love your food!
Well, yeah. What are you having, Akimizu?

Let me see... Now that you ask,
I really have to think about it...
By the way, is there any food you don't like?

Let me see, not really...
Oh! There is one! A food I can't stand!
Huh? What is it?

Um, it's called "sashimi"...
It's all squishy, and on top of that it has
this fishy smell. I just can't handle it...

Huh~, I see.
But it doesn't seem like you'd get
many chances to eat it anyway.

That's true. If they served it at Silver Moon
or someplace, I'd faint for sure!
rows.notes: Silver Moon: glossary status provisional. The Japanese quotation marks around the name are dropped, as in other finished rows (c00580).

rows.en:
Th-That's never gonna happen,
so don't worry...

(So she can't handle "sashimi".
That's so girly.)

(Well, it's almost lunchtime.
What should I have...?)

\p-chan,
what's wrong? You look like you're
worried about something.

Oh, yeah, I was just wondering
what to eat for lunch...
Yeah, I guess so. What are you having, Yuu?
By the way, is there any food you don't like?

Huh~, I see.
But it doesn't seem like you'd get
many chances to eat it anyway.

Th-That's never gonna happen,
so don't worry...

(So she can't handle "sashimi"...
That's so Yuu.)

uncertain: c20447: 'Good work, \p-kun.' is used three times in nml_yuu_006, once as a closing line in the female branch where the player is addressed -kun (the female opening c20456 uses -chan); kept -kun as written, likely a script slip.
